h: A working test bench for Bricks Productivity
pages.x: BRXProd playground A working test bench for Bricks Productivity Every page here exercises one part of the BRXProd system, built to the house standards. Everything you read is demo content. Explore the design system See the components What's on this site Each card opens a page that shows one feature in use. The whole card is the link (brxp-clickable-box). Design system Layout Rails Named grid lines replace max-widths: content, wide, breakout, layout and full. Design system Surfaces & Colour Four Surfaces paint every panel; the a11y tokens keep text readable on each. Design system Corners Inverted and outset radius utilities, driven by mask and pseudo-elements. Building blocks Components Buttons from their own controls, generic BEM cards, clickable boxes and focus rings. Building blocks Carousel Slider (Nestable) with BRXProd's Splide extensions: autoplay, a gallery and a ticker. Motion Motion GSAP Prompt Library effects, each in its own snippet, loaded by the GSAP Loader. Built to the house standards BEM classes with a Settings block, container queries instead of media queries, semantic HTML and text colours that always come from the a11y tokens. This band is painted with Surface 4. Open the Style Guide

Carousel Slider (Nestable), extended Every carousel on a BRXProd site is Bricks' Slider (Nestable) with the Splide Extensions snippet: never hand-written carousel JS. Autoplay that pauses off-screen Three fictional testimonials. The Intersection extension stops autoplay while the slider is out of view; arrows and dots stay keyboard-operable. The rails meant we stopped arguing about max-widths. Every section just names the rail it wants. — Alex Example, fictional front-end lead Switching the whole site to dark took four Surface variables and one palette change. — Sam Placeholder, fictional designer Snippets with names and on/off switches beat code hidden in a Code element every time. — Jordan Sample, fictional developer Image gallery Three photos per view on wide screens, fewer as the screen narrows (Splide breakpoints), looping with keyboard-operable arrows and dots. Ticker with AutoScroll The AutoScroll extension turns a slider into a continuous strip. It is decorative, so the wrapper is hidden from assistive technology, and it stays still for reduced-motion visitors.

h: The whole card is the link
pages.x: Components Generic blocks, styled once Buttons take their look only from their own controls and the theme style. Cards are one generic block whatever they show. Buttons Every style and size comes from the Button element's controls; there is no button CSS anywhere on the site. Primary Secondary Light Dark Muted Info Success Warning Danger Size sm Size md Size lg Size xl Primary outline Secondary outline Cards One card-v2 block with an optional image. What changes is content, a Surface class, or a BRXProd utility. Default A plain card Kicker, title, text and a Button. The button sits at the bottom because the text grows, not because the button is styled. Open the carousel Line clamp Long text, three lines brxp-line-clamp with brxp-line-clamp--3 cuts this paragraph after three lines however long it gets. It keeps cards in a row the same height when the copy varies from a sentence to a short essay, which is exactly what happens once real content arrives. Clickable box + focus The whole card is the link Tab to it: brxp-focus-here draws the focus ring around the card, not just the title.

h: Scoops and flares in pure CSS
pages.x: Corners Scoops and flares in pure CSS BRXProd's corner utilities cut inverted corners with a mask and add outset flares with a pseudo-element. Inverted radius A mask scoops each corner into the element. Combine as many corners as you like; tune the size with --inverted-radius. brxp-inverted-radius-top-left-horizontal brxp-inverted-radius-top-right-horizontal brxp-inverted-radius-bottom-left-horizontal brxp-inverted-radius-bottom-right-horizontal All four corners at once Corners on images The same mask works on an image: put the corner classes on the Image element itself. brxp-inverted-radius-top-left-horizontal. Photo: Steven Spassov / Unsplash. brxp-inverted-radius-bottom-right-horizontal. Photo: Florian Klauer / Unsplash. All four inverted corners at once. Photo: Linh Nguyen / Unsplash. Outset radius A pseudo-element flares out of the corner into the parent. Here the tab's bottom-right corner curves into its panel; --outset-color matches the tab. brxp-outset-radius-bottom-right-horizontal The panel joins the tab without a seam. Use at most two outset classes per element: one -horizontal (::before) and one -vertical (::after).

Layout Rails Named rails, not max-widths brxp-rails turns a section into a grid with named lines. Children sit on the content rail and choose a wider one by class. Symmetric spans One utility class per rail, and nothing else: no width, no max-width, no negative margins. Content rail (the default) brxp-rail-wide brxp-rail-breakout brxp-rail-layout brxp-rail-full: edge to edge, inline padding stripped brxp-rail-full + brxp-gutter-x: edge to edge with the gutters back Asymmetric spans When an element starts on one rail and ends on another, it gets ID-level CSS naming the lines, never a new class. content-start → full-end, set with ID-level CSS layout-start → content-end, set with ID-level CSS Images on rails Figures pick a rail exactly like any other child. The second one runs edge to edge on the full rail, with its caption's gutters put back by brxp-gutter-x. brxp-rail-breakout: a little wider than the text column. Photo: Charlie Foster / Unsplash. brxp-rail-full with the media-figure--flush modifier: square corners and an ultrawide crop. Photo: Anton Sulsky / Unsplash. Background media brxp-has-bg-media on the section and brxp-has-bg-media__media on the image: the photo fills the band and is hidden from assistive technology.

h: GSAP, one smooth effect per snippet
pages.x: Motion GSAP, one smooth effect per snippet Effects come from the GSAP Prompt Library and load through BRXProd's GSAP Loader. Each sits in its own snippet so it can be switched off alone. Magnetic button: move your cursor close UI-01 Card Hover Lift Hover a card: it rises and its shadow deepens. Reduced-motion visitors get the end state instantly. Effect Rise Moves up 8px with transform, so layout never shifts. Effect Scale Grows by 2%, just enough to feel lifted. Effect Shadow The shadow deepens as the card leaves the page. ADV-15 Organic Floating Elements Each shape drifts to a new random point, rotation and scale on every cycle, so no two loops match. Decorative, and still for reduced motion. T-16 and the sliding nav The page title's shimmer is T-16 Shine Sweep. Narrow the window and open the menu: the header's Nav Menu uses BRXProd's sliding drill-down with the GSAP glide effect.

It guides the eye, sets the pace and lets the words do the talking. This sample shows how headings, body text, links and quotes sit together on a real page. Hierarchy Creates Momentum Headings tell the reader what matters first, and body copy carries the story. Use bold for emphasis , italics for nuance , and links that stand out without shouting . Rhythm and Space Line length, line height and the space between paragraphs set the reading rhythm: Keep lines between 45 and 75 characters. Give headings more space above than below. Use one link style everywhere. A well-set page doesn’t ask for attention. It earns it, one line at a time. Surfaces & Colour Four Surfaces, one dark theme Panels are painted with the brxp-surface classes, not hand-picked colours, so the whole site re-themes from four sets of variables. The four Surfaces Each card carries one Surface class. Text and links take that Surface's own colours, all above 4.5:1. brxp-surface1 Page / section The page itself follows Surface 1, so a re-theme of the Surfaces moves the page too. Sample link brxp-surface2 Raised card / panel Cards and panels sit one step lighter than the page. Sample link brxp-surface3 Inset well Wells and the footer sit one step darker.
